# GitHub settings for the CI/CD and infrastructure workflows.
# Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions, and Settings > Environments.
#
# Workflows:
#   deploy.yml           every branch push: build -> unit -> e2e (k3s on the runner)
#                        main only: push :sha-<commit> tags, then deploy to EKS
#                        (job "Deploy to EKS", environment: production)
#   infra-apply.yml      manual: terraform plan -> approval -> apply + cluster add-ons
#                        (plan: environment production, apply: production-infra)
#   infra-destroy.yml    manual: type the cluster name, approval, teardown + destroy
#                        (environment: production-infra)
#   market-hours.yml     08:17 / 16:07 IST Mon-Fri: market-mode.sh auto (needs PROD_DEPLOY_ENABLED)
#                        (environment: production)
#   cleanup-branch-images.yml  branch deleted -> delete its Docker Hub tags
#
# AWS access uses GitHub OIDC (no AWS keys stored). The role is created once
# by terraform/bootstrap and trusts only this repo's production and
# production-infra environments.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Environments (Settings > Environments)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#   production        used by the EKS deploy and terraform plan (no reviewers needed)
#                     optional: deployment branch rule = main
#   production-infra  used by terraform apply and destroy
#                     add Required reviewers; deployment branch rule = main

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Repository secrets
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
DOCKERHUB_USERNAME=prabuselvamnatarajan
DOCKERHUB_TOKEN=your_docker_hub_personal_access_token_here

# Contents of Secret moneymaker-secrets in prod, as KEY=value lines.
# Generate it locally with random values:  ./scripts/aws/generate-prod-secrets.sh
# Every key below is required; the passwords inside the URIs must match.
# Mongo's root user and Redis's requirepass both read this Secret. Changing them after Mongo has
# initialised its data volume does not change the existing Mongo root password.
PROD_APP_SECRETS=<<multi-line value>>
#   MONGO_ROOT_USERNAME=root
#   MONGO_ROOT_PASSWORD=change-me
#   MONGO_URI=mongodb://root:change-me@mongo1:27017,mongo2:27017,mongo3:27017/?replicaSet=rs0&authSource=admin
#   MONGODB_URI=mongodb://root:change-me@mongo1:27017,mongo2:27017,mongo3:27017/?replicaSet=rs0&authSource=admin
#   REDIS_PASSWORD=change-me-too
#   REDIS_URL=redis://:change-me-too@redis:6379
#   JWT_ACCESS_SECRET=random
#   JWT_REFRESH_SECRET=random
#   BACKTEST_SERVICE_TOKEN=random
#   ME_CONFIG_MONGODB_ADMINUSERNAME=root
#   ME_CONFIG_MONGODB_ADMINPASSWORD=change-me
#   ME_CONFIG_MONGODB_URL=mongodb://root:change-me@mongo1:27017,mongo2:27017,mongo3:27017/?replicaSet=rs0&authSource=admin

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Repository variables (not secret)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
AWS_ROLE_ARN=arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/moneymaker-github-actions   # terraform/bootstrap output
TF_STATE_BUCKET=moneymaker-tfstate-CHANGE-ME                            # terraform/bootstrap output
AWS_REGION=ap-south-1                                                   # optional, default ap-south-1
EKS_CLUSTER_NAME=moneymaker-prod                                        # optional, default moneymaker-prod
EKS_ADMIN_ARNS=["arn:aws:iam::123456789012:user/you"]                   # optional JSON list: extra kubectl admins
PROD_DEPLOY_ENABLED=true                                                # set after the first Infrastructure Apply
